# Otaru slope: research for the route (step 4)

Status: **research preview**. Nobody has reviewed this yet. The street in the
game is **illustrative**: it mixes building types from Sakaimachi, Ironai and
the canal. It does not copy any real street. Names are generic. No real shop
names, logos or brands are shown in the game.

Sources are mostly the Japan Tourism Agency's multilingual commentary
database (MLIT "tagengo-db"). These are official, short texts, and each page
can be checked online. Where sources do not agree, or where I could not check
a point, the text says **Unsure**.

## The place

- Sakaimachi, Ironai, Kitahama and Minamihama were built on reclaimed land in
  1889. Merchants then built stores and warehouses on Sakaimachi, and barges
  moored in front of them, before canal work started in 1914.
  ([MLIT R5-00029](https://www.mlit.go.jp/tagengo-db/en/R5-00029.html))
- Herring fertilizer was the big trade. It went to cotton and indigo fields in
  southwestern Honshu. The annual herring catch in the late 19th century was
  "close to 90,000 tons". ([MLIT R5-00029](https://www.mlit.go.jp/tagengo-db/en/R5-00029.html))
- The canal was built from 1914 to 1923 (Taishō era, not Meiji). Today a
  walkway and gas lamps line it.
  ([MLIT R5-00045](https://www.mlit.go.jp/tagengo-db/en/R5-00045.html))
- Old photos show suited bankers, customers in kimono, horse carts,
  rickshaws and sometimes a car.
  ([MLIT R5-00029](https://www.mlit.go.jp/tagengo-db/en/R5-00029.html))

**Unsure, about the slope:** Sakaimachi Street runs along the old shoreline
and is not very steep. The steep part of Otaru is the hills behind it, with
streets that go down toward the canal. A long, steep, icy shopping street
with all 12 types is a game liberty. Label the scene as illustrative.

## The 12 buildings, top of the slope to the canal

Each entry has: the generic name for the game, 2 short history sentences, the
source, and a short wall-label line for the caption card (step 5).

### 1. Merchant House with Fire Walls
Stone merchant stores in Sakaimachi had fireproof features, because fire was a
large risk to the stock. One store of about 1895 has *udatsu* fire walls at
the front (stone walls capped with roof tiles) and plastered fireproof
shutters on the upper storage floor.
Source: [MLIT R5-00032, Former Kaneko Motosaburo Store](https://www.mlit.go.jp/tagengo-db/en/R5-00032.html)
Label: "Merchant house, c. 1895. Stone, roof tiles, fire walls."
**Unsure:** the English page says "around 1895", not an exact year.

### 2. Clock Shop with a Band Balcony
An early-20th-century clock and watch store was a two-storey timber frame clad
in tuff stone, with ceramic *shachihoko* on the roof ridge. A brass band in
red-and-white uniforms played on its large balcony to bring in customers.
Source: [MLIT R5-00031, Former Iwanaga Clock Store](https://www.mlit.go.jp/tagengo-db/en/R5-00031.html)
Label: "Clock shop, early 20th century. Tuff stone, arched doors, a balcony for the band."

### 3. Rice Merchant
A rice dealer's building from 1912 is a two-storey brick building. Later it
was a furniture store, and today it holds a music box museum.
Sources: [MLIT R5-00029](https://www.mlit.go.jp/tagengo-db/en/R5-00029.html),
[Studio Sakyo pop-up card, Former Kyosei Company](https://studio-sakyo.jp/popup/01hokkaido/03douou/kyosei/kyosei-company_en.html)
Label: "Rice merchant, 1912. Brick, two storeys."
**Unsure:** Wikipedia says the music box museum's main building dates from
1902 ([Otaru Music Box Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otaru_Music_Box_Museum)).
It may be a different building. Use "1912" only for the rice dealer.

### 4. Wholesale Store
Wholesalers of sugar, cotton and rice traded on Sakaimachi in the boom years.
Ships brought goods from Honshu and took herring fertilizer back.
Sources: [MLIT R5-00029](https://www.mlit.go.jp/tagengo-db/en/R5-00029.html),
[MLIT R5-00045](https://www.mlit.go.jp/tagengo-db/en/R5-00045.html)
Label: "Wholesale store. Sugar, cotton, rice. Snow, free of charge."
**Unsure:** no single wholesale building was checked; this is a generic type.

### 5. Glass Workshop
A glass maker was founded in Otaru in 1901. It first made oil lamps, then
fishing-net floats and tableware, and by the 1920s it had about 400 workers.
Sources: [MLIT R5-00017](https://www.mlit.go.jp/tagengo-db/en/R5-00017.html),
[Domingo, 2022](https://domingo.ne.jp/en/article/12444)
Label: "Glass workshop, from 1901. Oil lamps, net floats, a great deal of heat."

### 6. Herring Fertilizer Warehouse
A family built a stone warehouse in the 1890s to store herring fertilizer.
Volcanic-stone walls sit on a fir and spruce frame, and handcarts ran on rails
through a stone corridor inside.
Source: [MLIT R5-00017, Former Kimura Warehouse](https://www.mlit.go.jp/tagengo-db/en/R5-00017.html)
Label: "Stone warehouse, 1890s. Volcanic stone on a timber frame. Cart rails inside."
**Unsure:** MLIT gives 1894; [Domingo](https://domingo.ne.jp/en/article/12444)
and [Atlas Obscura](https://www.atlasobscura.com/places/kitaichi-hall-japan)
give 1891 for a building at the same address. Say "1890s".

### 7. Lamp-Lit Hall
Today, one old warehouse is a café lit only by 167 glass oil lamps. Staff
light them by hand every morning.
Sources: [MLIT R5-00017](https://www.mlit.go.jp/tagengo-db/en/R5-00017.html),
[Atlas Obscura](https://www.atlasobscura.com/places/kitaichi-hall-japan)
Label: "Lamp hall. 167 oil lamps, lit by hand. Not by you."
**Unsure:** this is a modern use (the building opened as a shop in 1983).
Show it as present-day, not as boom-era.

### 8. Bank
Banks in Otaru grew from three in 1887 to sixteen in 1907. They built in
classical stone styles to look rich and safe, and the central bank's branch of
1912 has turrets.
Sources: [MLIT R5-00029](https://www.mlit.go.jp/tagengo-db/en/R5-00029.html),
[MLIT R5-00027, Ironai Banking District](https://www.mlit.go.jp/tagengo-db/en/R5-00027.html)
Label: "Bank, 1910s. Stone columns. Your deposit was not accepted."
**Unsure:** the banks stand on Ironai, the street next to Sakaimachi. Other
MLIT pages say "some 25 banks" in the district over time.

### 9. Shipowner's Warehouse with Roof Creatures
Merchant shipowners from the Kaga region built a warehouse in 1890 around a
courtyard for unloading cargo. Eight tiled *shachihoko* sit on its ridges,
which is rare outside castles.
Source: [MLIT R5-00015, Former Otaru Warehouse](https://www.mlit.go.jp/tagengo-db/en/R5-00015.html)
Label: "Shipowner's warehouse, 1890. Eight roof creatures, all watching."

### 10. Shipping House with a Painted Mark
Shipowner families painted their own mark on warehouse fronts, store fronts
and staff uniforms. One family's mark was two parallel black lines.
Source: [MLIT R5-00013, Former Ukon Warehouse](https://www.mlit.go.jp/tagengo-db/en/R5-00013.html)
Label: "Shipping house, 1890s. Two black lines. Not a warning."
**Note:** use a made-up mark in the game, not the real family's mark.

### 11. Hotel
A hotel opened on the street in 1931 and reopened in 2019 after renovation.
Source: [MLIT R5-00029](https://www.mlit.go.jp/tagengo-db/en/R5-00029.html)
Label: "Hotel, 1931. Rooms available. Brakes not included."
**Unsure:** 1931 is Shōwa era, after the herring boom. Do not call it a boom
building.

### 12. Canal Warehouse (the finish)
The canal-side warehouses stand on land reclaimed after the canal was
finished in 1923. One stone warehouse with a timber frame dates from 1925.
Sources: [MLIT R5-00047, Warehouses along Otaru Canal](https://www.mlit.go.jp/tagengo-db/R5-00047.html),
[MLIT R5-00045](https://www.mlit.go.jp/tagengo-db/en/R5-00045.html)
Label: "Canal warehouse, 1925. Stone and timber. The end of the line."

## Street details for the art (step 6)

- **Roofs:** tile ridges with *shachihoko* on a few richer buildings (R5-00031,
  R5-00015). Snow on roofs and icicles are a winter look, not from a source.
- **Fire walls:** *udatsu* on a few merchant fronts (R5-00032).
- **Marks and signs:** painted family marks on fronts (R5-00013); one company
  used a "standing drum" mark (R5-00047). Use made-up marks.
- **Lighting:** oil lamps were made locally from 1901 (R5-00017). The canal
  has gas lamps today (R5-00045).
  **Unsure:** I did not find a source that the street had gas lamps in the
  boom years. Show lamps as part of the present-day street.
- **Street life (boom years):** horse carts, rickshaws, kimono, suits
  (R5-00029). Today: tourists with cameras.
- **January:** **Unsure.** Otaru is very snowy in January, but I did not
  check a measured number. The candle festival (Snow Light Path) is in
  February ([Sapporo Travel](https://www.sapporo.travel/en/event/event-list/otaru-snow-light-path/)),
  so do not show it in January.
- **Do not show as boom-era:** the steam clock at the south end of the street
  is modern (made by a Canadian clockmaker, sister to Vancouver's steam
  clock; [GOOD LUCK TRIP](https://www.gltjp.com/en/review/item/16886/)).
  **Unsure:** its install year is not checked.
  Music box shops and the glass shops' tourist trade are modern too.
